sourceReview.notes: The hardest mental model in the complete article is why ReLU changes the required weight scale and why a modest one-layer mismatch becomes severe with depth. Under the standard independent, zero-mean, symmetric preactivation assumptions, define q_l as the activation second moment E[x_l squared]. If fan-in times Var(W) equals c, the linear map multiplies q by c and ReLU retains half of that second moment, so q_l/q_(l-1) equals c/2. The original visual calculates four repeated layers for c equal to 1, 2, and 3: final ratios 1/16, 1, and 81/16, plotted on an explicitly labelled logarithmic vertical scale so equal multiplicative changes have equal spacing. It deliberately says second moment rather than variance because ReLU outputs are not zero-mean.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description containing the assumptions, all three per-layer multipliers, and exact four-layer outcomes. Direct labels, vertical position, distinct point shapes, and solid, dashed, or dotted strokes preserve every comparison without color. A 360-unit viewBox scales fluidly with no minimum width or horizontal scrolling at 390 CSS pixels. Established theme variables provide dark and light contrast, and shared print rules force a light high-contrast canvas and keep the figure together.
